records.source: חַכְמ֣וֹת נָ֭שִׁים בָּנְתָ֣ה בֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝אִוֶּ֗לֶת בְּיָדֶ֥יהָ תֶהֶרְסֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: [The] wise of women builds her house, but folly with her hands tears it down.
pieces: A wise woman builds up her home, \q but a foolish one pulls it down with her own hands.

L.1: [The] wise among women builds her house, \q but folly tears it down with her own hands.

R.1: A wise woman makes her home strong. \q A foolish woman destroys her own home.

decisions.choice: wise women ... folly: a wise woman and a foolish one
decisions.reason: The text reads "the wise of women" and then "folly" as subject. It may recall Wisdom who built her house (9:1) and Folly (9:13), seen in ordinary women's lives.

records.source: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּ֭יָשְׁרוֹ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּנְל֖וֹז דְּרָכָ֣יו בּוֹזֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: [One] walking in his uprightness fears YHWH, but [one] crooked [in] his ways despises him.
pieces: Whoever lives uprightly fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q but whoever goes crooked ways despises {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.2: Whoever walks in {{gender:their|his}} uprightness fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q but whoever is devious in {{gender:their|his}} ways despises {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.2: People who live honestly show that they honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q People who are dishonest show that they hate {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: fears ... despises: how one lives shows how one regards God
decisions.reason: A person's way of life is a statement about God (14:31; 17:5).

records.source: בְּֽפִי־אֱ֭וִיל חֹ֣טֶר גַּאֲוָ֑ה וְשִׂפְתֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תִּשְׁמוּרֵֽם׃
records.gloss: In [the] mouth of a fool [is] a rod of pride, but [the] lips of wise [people] will preserve them.
pieces: A fool's talk is a rod for his own back, the fruit of his pride, \q but the words of the wise keep them safe.

L.3: In [the] mouth of a fool [is] a rod of pride, \q but [the] lips of [the] wise will preserve them.

R.3: Proud fools get themselves into trouble by what they say. \q The words of wise people keep them safe.

decisions.choice: a rod of pride: a shoot of pride, or a rod for pride
decisions.reason: The word (hoter) is a shoot or branch (Isaiah 11:1), or a rod. The fool's proud words either grow from pride or bring a beating on him.

records.source: בְּאֵ֣ין אֲ֭לָפִים אֵב֣וּס בָּ֑ר וְרָב־תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּכֹ֣חַ שֽׁוֹר׃
records.gloss: When there are no oxen, [the] manger [is] clean, but much produce [is] by [the] strength of an ox.
pieces: Without oxen the feeding trough stays clean, \q but it takes a strong ox to bring a big harvest.

L.4: Where [there are] no oxen, [the] manger [is] clean, \q but much harvest [comes] by [the] strength of an ox.

R.4: If you do not own oxen, you do not have to clean up after them. \q But you need strong oxen to grow a big crop.

decisions.choice: oxen ... harvest: work animals bring mess and gain
decisions.reason: Oxen pulled the plow. They cost food and cleaning, but without them there is little harvest.

records.source: עֵ֣ד אֱ֭מוּנִים לֹ֣א יְכַזֵּ֑ב וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.
pieces: An honest witness does not deceive, \q but a false witness pours out lies.

L.5: A faithful witness does not lie, \q but a false witness breathes out lies.

R.5: An honest witness does not lie in court. \q A dishonest witness tells one lie after another.

decisions.choice: witness: in court, as in 12:17

records.source: בִּקֶּשׁ־לֵ֣ץ חָכְמָ֣ה וָאָ֑יִן וְדַ֖עַת לְנָב֣וֹן נָקָֽל׃
records.gloss: A mocker seeks wisdom, and there is none, but knowledge to [one] understanding [is] easy.
pieces: A mocker goes looking for wisdom and comes up empty, \q but a person of understanding learns with ease.

L.6: A mocker seeks wisdom and [finds] none, \q but knowledge [comes] easily to [one who] understands.

R.6: People who make fun of others cannot find wisdom, even if they look for it. \q But learning is easy for people who understand.

decisions.choice: a mocker seeks wisdom: but not humbly
decisions.reason: The mocker wants wisdom without being corrected (9:7–8), so it eludes him.

records.source: לֵ֣ךְ מִ֭נֶּגֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּסִ֑יל וּבַל־יָ֝דַ֗עְתָּ שִׂפְתֵי־דָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: Go from before a foolish person, and you will not have known lips of knowledge.
pieces: Stay away from a fool, \q for you will not hear knowledge from his lips.

L.7: Go from [the] presence of a foolish person, \q for you will not find lips of knowledge [there].

R.7: Stay away from foolish people. \q You will not learn anything from them.

decisions.choice: you will not have known: there is nothing to learn there
decisions.reason: The second line may say why to leave (you will find no knowledge) or what happens if you stay.

records.source: חָכְמַ֣ת עָ֭רוּם הָבִ֣ין דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְאִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] wisdom of a prudent [person] [is] to understand his way, but [the] folly of fools [is] deceit.
pieces: The prudent are wise because they think about where they are going, \q but the folly of fools is self-deception.

L.8: [The] wisdom of [the] prudent [is] to understand {{gender:their|his}} way, \q but [the] folly of fools [is] deceit.

R.8: Wise people think carefully about how they live. \q Foolish people fool themselves.

decisions.choice: deceit: deceiving themselves, or others
decisions.reason: The fool's folly misleads, most of all the fool himself (verse 12).

records.source: אֱ֭וִלִים יָלִ֣יץ אָשָׁ֑ם וּבֵ֖ין יְשָׁרִ֣ים רָצֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Fools mock guilt, but among [the] upright [is] favor.
pieces: Fools make light of guilt, \q but among the upright there is goodwill.

L.9: Fools mock at guilt, \q but among [the] upright [there is] favor.

R.9: Fools laugh when they do wrong and do not try to make it right. \q Good people want to make peace.

decisions.choice: guilt: guilt, or the offering to make amends
decisions.reason: The word (asham) is guilt and also the offering to set it right (Leviticus 5:15). Fools scoff at making amends; the upright seek goodwill.

decisions.choice: fools mock: a singular verb with a plural subject
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, perhaps "each fool mocks".

records.source: לֵ֗ב י֭וֹדֵעַ מָרַּ֣ת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּ֝בְשִׂמְחָת֗וֹ לֹא־יִתְעָ֥רַב זָֽר׃
records.gloss: A heart knows [the] bitterness of its soul, and in its joy a stranger does not share.
pieces: Each heart knows its own sorrow, \q and no outsider can share its joy.

L.10: [The] heart knows its own bitterness, \q and in its joy a stranger does not share.

R.10: Only you know how sad you really are. \q No one else can fully share your happiness either.

decisions.choice: each heart alone: the privacy of feeling
decisions.reason: A saying about how much each person carries alone, in sorrow and in joy.

records.source: בֵּ֣ית רְ֭שָׁעִים יִשָּׁמֵ֑ד וְאֹ֖הֶל יְשָׁרִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיחַ׃
records.gloss: [The] house of wicked [people] will be destroyed, but [the] tent of upright [people] will flourish.
pieces: The house of the wicked will be wiped out, \q but the tent of the upright will thrive.

L.11: [The] house of [the] wicked will be destroyed, \q but [the] tent of [the] upright will flourish.

R.11: The homes of evil people will be destroyed. \q The homes of good people will do well.

decisions.choice: house ... tent: a solid house against a tent
decisions.reason: The irony: the wicked's house falls, while the upright's tent stands (12:7).

records.source: יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי־מָֽוֶת׃
records.gloss: There is a way right before a person, but its end [is the] ways of death.
pieces: There is a road that looks right to a person, \q but at the end of it is death.

L.12: There is a way [that seems] right to a person, \q but its end [is the] way to death.

R.12: Some ways of living seem right to people, \q but they lead to death.

decisions.choice: repeated in 16:25
decisions.reason: The same saying returns in 16:25. Compare 12:15 and 3:7.

records.source: גַּם־בִּשְׂח֥וֹק יִכְאַב־לֵ֑ב וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּשִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה׃
records.gloss: Even in laughter a heart is in pain, and its end, joy, [is] grief.
pieces: Even while laughing the heart may ache, \q and joy can end in sorrow.

L.13: Even in laughter [the] heart may ache, \q and [the] end of joy [may be] grief.

R.13: Sometimes people laugh even when they are sad. \q And happiness can turn to sadness.

decisions.choice: laughter ... grief: feelings mixed and passing
decisions.reason: Compare verse 10 and Ecclesiastes 7:3–4.

records.source: מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: From his ways will be satisfied [the] backslider of heart, and from himself a good person.
pieces: The faithless will get their fill of their own ways, \q and the good will be rewarded for theirs.

L.14: [The] backslider in heart will be filled with {{gender:their|his}} own ways, \q and a good person [with what is] {{gender:their|his}} own.

R.14: People who turn away from God will get what they deserve. \q Good people will be rewarded for the good they do.

decisions.choice: backslider in heart: one who has turned away
decisions.reason: The word (sug) means to turn back or away (Psalm 80:19).

decisions.choice: from himself: from his own deeds
alternatives: from above him (with a small change)
decisions.reason: "From upon himself" is unusual; it most likely means from his own conduct.

records.source: פֶּ֭תִי יַאֲמִ֣ין לְכָל־דָּבָ֑ר וְ֝עָר֗וּם יָבִ֥ין לַאֲשֻׁרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A simple [person] believes every word, but a prudent [person] considers his step.
pieces: The naive believe everything they hear, \q but the prudent watch where they are going.

L.15: [The] simple believes every word, \q but [the] prudent considers {{gender:their|his}} steps.

R.15: Foolish people believe everything they hear. \q Wise people think carefully before they act.

decisions.choice: the simple believes everything: the definition of 1:4
decisions.reason: This is what makes the simple simple.

records.source: חָכָ֣ם יָ֭רֵא וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וּ֝כְסִ֗יל מִתְעַבֵּ֥ר וּבוֹטֵֽחַ׃
records.gloss: A wise [person] fears and turns from evil, but a fool is arrogant and confident.
pieces: The wise are careful and turn away from evil, \q but a fool is reckless and overconfident.

L.16: [The] wise is cautious and turns from evil, \q but a fool is reckless and sure of himself.

R.16: Wise people are careful and stay away from evil. \q Fools rush ahead without thinking.

decisions.choice: fears: is cautious, or fears the LORD
decisions.reason: "Fears" here may mean caution, or the fear of the LORD (3:7).

decisions.choice: reckless: overbearing, carried away
decisions.reason: The verb (hitabber) means to be overbearing or to fly into a rage (20:2; 26:17).

records.source: קְֽצַר־אַ֭פַּיִם יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אִוֶּ֑לֶת וְאִ֥ישׁ מְ֝זִמּ֗וֹת יִשָּׂנֵֽא׃
records.gloss: [One] short of anger does folly, and a person of schemes is hated.
pieces: Someone with a short temper acts foolishly, \q and the one who schemes is hated.

L.17: [One] quick-tempered does folly, \q and a person of schemes is hated.

R.17: People who get angry quickly do foolish things. \q People who plan evil are hated.

decisions.choice: short of anger: quick-tempered
decisions.reason: "Short of nostrils" is quick to anger; "long of nostrils" (verse 29) is patient.

records.source: נָחֲל֣וּ פְתָאיִ֣ם אִוֶּ֑לֶת וַֽ֝עֲרוּמִ֗ים יַכְתִּ֥רוּ דָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: Simple [people] inherit folly, but prudent [people] are crowned [with] knowledge.
pieces: The naive end up with folly as their inheritance, \q but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

L.18: [The] simple inherit folly, \q but [the] prudent are crowned [with] knowledge.

R.18: Foolish people end up even more foolish. \q Wise people end up with more knowledge.

decisions.choice: crowned: surrounded, or crowned
decisions.reason: The verb (katar) means to surround, and in this form to crown (Psalm 142:8).

records.source: שַׁח֣וּ רָ֭עִים לִפְנֵ֣י טוֹבִ֑ים וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים עַֽל־שַׁעֲרֵ֥י צַדִּֽיק׃
records.gloss: Evil [people] bow before good [people], and wicked [people] at [the] gates of [the] righteous.
pieces: In the end the evil bow low to the good, \q and the wicked come begging at the doors of the righteous.

L.19: [The] evil bow before [the] good, \q and [the] wicked at [the] gates of [the] righteous.

R.19: In the end, evil people will bow down to good people.

decisions.choice: bow at the gates: come begging
decisions.reason: The picture is of the wicked coming to the doors of the righteous for help (1 Samuel 2:36).

records.source: גַּם־לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ יִשָּׂ֣נֵא רָ֑שׁ וְאֹהֲבֵ֖י עָשִׁ֣יר רַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Even by his neighbor [the] poor is hated, but those loving [the] rich [are] many.
pieces: The poor are shunned even by their neighbors, \q but the rich have plenty of friends.

L.20: [The] poor is disliked even by {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, \q but [the] rich [have] many friends.

R.20: Poor people are not liked even by their neighbors. \q But rich people have many friends.

decisions.choice: an observation, not approval
decisions.reason: The saying states how people behave (19:4, 7). Verse 21 gives God's view.

records.source: בָּז־לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ חוֹטֵ֑א וּמְחוֹנֵ֖ן עֲנָוִ֣ים אַשְׁרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: [One] despising his neighbor sins, but [one] showing favor [to the] humble, how blessed [is] he.
pieces: To look down on a neighbor is a sin, \q but how blessed is the one who is kind to the humble.

L.21: Whoever despises {{gender:their|his}} neighbor sins, \q but whoever is kind to [the] humble, how blessed [is] {{gender:that one|he}}.

R.21: It is wrong to look down on your neighbor. \q God blesses people who are kind to humble people.

decisions.choice: the humble, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: As in 3:34, the written consonants (ketiv) read "the poor" and the scribes' reading (qere) "the humble"; the two are often the same people in Scripture.

decisions.choice: how blessed: as in 3:13
decisions.reason: Verse 21 answers verse 20: God sees the poor differently.

records.source: הֲֽלוֹא־יִ֭תְעוּ חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע וְחֶ֥סֶד וֶ֝אֱמֶ֗ת חֹ֣רְשֵׁי טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: Do not [those] devising evil go astray? But loyalty and faithfulness [belong to those] devising good.
pieces: Surely those who plot evil go astray, \q but those who plan good find loyal love and faithfulness.

L.22: Do not those who plot evil go astray? \q But loyal love and faithfulness [belong to] those who plan good.

R.22: People who plan to do evil lose their way. \q People who plan to do good are loved and trusted.

decisions.choice: loyal love and faithfulness: as in 3:3
decisions.reason: They may be shown to those who plan good, by God and others, or be their own character.

records.source: בְּכָל־עֶ֭צֶב יִהְיֶ֣ה מוֹתָ֑ר וּדְבַר־שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: In all toil there is profit, but [the] word of lips [leads] only to lack.
pieces: All hard work brings a profit, \q but mere talk leads only to poverty.

L.23: In all toil there is profit, \q but mere talk [leads] only to poverty.

R.23: If you work hard, you will gain something. \q If you only talk, you will end up poor.

decisions.choice: a word of lips: empty talk
decisions.reason: Talk with no work behind it (2 Kings 18:20).

records.source: עֲטֶ֣רֶת חֲכָמִ֣ים עָשְׁרָ֑ם אִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
records.gloss: [The] crown of wise [people] [is] their wealth; [the] folly of fools [is] folly.
pieces: Wealth is a crown for the wise, \q but the folly of fools brings only folly.

L.24: [The] crown of [the] wise [is] their wealth; \q [the] folly of fools [is] folly.

R.24: Wise people are honored for what they have. \q Fools only become more foolish.

decisions.choice: folly is folly: fools gain nothing but more folly
alternatives: the garland of fools is folly (with a small change)
decisions.reason: The repetition is striking. Many read "the garland of fools is folly" to match the crown of the first line.

records.source: מַצִּ֣יל נְ֭פָשׁוֹת עֵ֣ד אֱמֶ֑ת וְיָפִ֖חַ כְּזָבִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: A true witness delivers lives, but [one who] breathes out lies [is] deceit.
pieces: A truthful witness saves lives, \q but one who pours out lies is a traitor.

L.25: A true witness saves lives, \q but one who breathes out lies [is a] deceiver.

R.25: An honest witness can save someone's life. \q A witness who lies betrays people.

decisions.choice: saves lives: in a court case
decisions.reason: A life could depend on testimony (Deuteronomy 19:15–19).

records.source: בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מִבְטַח־עֹ֑ז וּ֝לְבָנָ֗יו יִהְיֶ֥ה מַחְסֶֽה׃
records.gloss: In [the] fear of YHWH [is] confidence of strength, and to his children there will be a refuge.
pieces: Whoever fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has a secure fortress, \q and their children will have a refuge.

L.26: In [the] fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] strong confidence, \q and for {{gender:their|his}} children there will be a refuge.

R.26: People who honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe feel safe. \q Their children will be safe too.

decisions.choice: his children: the children of the one who fears the LORD
decisions.reason: "His" most likely refers to the person who fears the LORD; it could refer to the LORD, whose children find refuge in him.

records.source: יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת׃
records.gloss: [The] fear of YHWH [is] a fountain of life, to turn aside from snares of death.
pieces: The fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a spring of life, \q steering people away from the traps of death.

L.27: [The] fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a fountain of life, \q to turn [one] aside from [the] snares of death.

R.27: Honoring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe gives life. \q It keeps people away from things that lead to death.

decisions.choice: as 13:14, with the fear of the LORD
decisions.reason: 13:14 says the same of the teaching of the wise.

records.source: בְּרָב־עָ֥ם הַדְרַת־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבְאֶ֥פֶס לְ֝אֹ֗ם מְחִתַּ֥ת רָזֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: In a multitude of people [is the] glory of a king, but in lack of people [is the] ruin of a ruler.
pieces: A king's glory is in having many people; \q without people a ruler is ruined.

L.28: In [the] multitude of people [is the] glory of a king, \q but without people a ruler [is] ruined.

R.28: A king is great when he rules many people. \q A ruler with no people has nothing.

decisions.choice: a king's glory: a large, thriving population
decisions.reason: A king's strength lay in his people; their well-being is his honor.

records.source: אֶ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם רַב־תְּבוּנָ֑ה וּקְצַר־ר֝֗וּחַ מֵרִ֥ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
records.gloss: [One] long of anger [has] great understanding, but [one] short of spirit exalts folly.
pieces: Patience shows great understanding, \q but a quick temper puts folly on display.

L.29: [One] slow to anger [has] great understanding, \q but [one] quick-tempered exalts folly.

R.29: People who are slow to get angry are very wise. \q People who get angry quickly show how foolish they are.

decisions.choice: long of anger: patient
decisions.reason: See verse 17.

records.source: חַיֵּ֣י בְ֭שָׂרִים לֵ֣ב מַרְפֵּ֑א וּרְקַ֖ב עֲצָמ֣וֹת קִנְאָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] life of [the] body [is] a heart of health, but rottenness of bones [is] envy.
pieces: A calm heart gives life to the body, \q but envy is decay in the bones.

L.30: A heart at peace [is the] life of [the] body, \q but envy [is] rot in [the] bones.

R.30: Being calm and at peace keeps your body healthy. \q But jealousy is like a disease that eats away your bones.

decisions.choice: envy: jealousy, passion
decisions.reason: The word (qinah) is jealousy or burning passion (6:34).

records.source: עֹ֣שֵֽׁקדָּ֭ל חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וּ֝מְכַבְּד֗וֹ חֹנֵ֥ן אֶבְיֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: [One] oppressing [the] poor insults his Maker, but [one] showing favor [to the] needy honors him.
pieces: Whoever oppresses the poor insults the One who made them, \q but kindness to the needy honors {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.31: Whoever oppresses [the] poor insults {{gender:their|his}} Maker, \q but whoever is kind to [the] needy honors {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.31: If you are cruel to poor people, you insult God, who made them. \q If you are kind to people in need, you honor God.

decisions.choice: his Maker: God, who made rich and poor
decisions.reason: God made the poor as he made everyone (22:2; Job 31:15). To oppress them is to insult him; to help them honors him (19:17; Matthew 25:40).

decisions.choice: his Maker: the oppressor's Maker or the poor man's
decisions.reason: "His" may point to the oppressor or to the poor. Either way, God is the Maker of both.

records.source: בְּֽ֭רָעָתוֹ יִדָּחֶ֣ה רָשָׁ֑ע וְחֹסֶ֖ה בְמוֹת֣וֹ צַדִּֽיק׃
records.gloss: By his wickedness a wicked [person] is thrust down, but [the] righteous [person] takes refuge in his death.
pieces: The wicked are brought down by their own evil, \q but the righteous have a refuge even in death.

L.32: [The] wicked is thrust down by {{gender:their|his}} wickedness, \q but [the] righteous takes refuge in {{gender:their|his}} death.

R.32: Evil people are destroyed by their own evil. \q But good people trust God even when they die.

decisions.choice: in his death, as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: in his integrity (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "in his integrity", which differs by two letters in Hebrew. As it stands, the Hebrew expresses hope beyond death.

decisions.choice: trust God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the refuge, which the Hebrew implies (14:26).

records.source: בְּלֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן תָּנ֣וּחַ חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְקֶ֥רֶב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים תִּוָּדֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: In [the] heart of [one] understanding wisdom rests, and in [the] inner part of fools it is made known.
pieces: Wisdom is at home in the heart of the discerning, \q and even among fools it makes itself known.

L.33: Wisdom rests in [the] heart of [one who] understands, \q and in [the] midst of fools it is made known.

R.33: Wisdom lives in the hearts of people who understand. \q Even fools can see it.

decisions.choice: it is made known: wisdom shows itself even among fools
alternatives: it is not known (the ancient Greek)
decisions.reason: The line is unclear. It may mean that wisdom is recognized even among fools, or (with the ancient Greek) that fools do not know it.

records.source: צְדָקָ֥ה תְרֽוֹמֵֽם־גּ֑וֹי וְחֶ֖סֶד לְאֻמִּ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃
records.gloss: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin [is] a disgrace to peoples.
pieces: Righteousness lifts a nation up, \q but sin brings disgrace on any people.

L.34: Righteousness exalts a nation, \q but sin [is] a disgrace to any people.

R.34: A nation becomes great when its people do what is right. \q Sin brings shame on any nation.

decisions.choice: disgrace: a different word from hesed, "loyal love"
decisions.reason: The word spelled hesed here is a rare word meaning shame or reproach (Leviticus 20:17), not the common word for loyal love.

records.source: רְֽצוֹן־מֶ֭לֶךְ לְעֶ֣בֶד מַשְׂכִּ֑יל וְ֝עֶבְרָת֗וֹ תִּהְיֶ֥ה מֵבִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: [The] favor of a king [is] for a servant acting wisely, but his fury [is for one] acting shamefully.
pieces: A king shows favor to a wise servant, \q but his anger falls on one who disgraces him.

L.35: A king's favor [goes] to a servant who acts wisely, \q but his wrath [falls on one] who acts shamefully.

R.35: A king is pleased with a servant who acts wisely. \q But he is angry with one who brings him shame.

decisions.choice: a king's servant: a royal official
decisions.reason: Many sayings in chapters 14–16 are about life at a king's court.
